$comment: Inkwire MCP tool surface, v1. Argument shapes are JSON-Schema-ish sketches — implement them in zod and generate the real JSON Schema from that. Every mutating tool returns the ids it touched plus graph_revision and layout_revision so the caller can tell whether to re-read.

conventions.board_scoping: Session-scoped current board, set by boards.open. Every canvas.* tool also accepts an explicit board_id which overrides it.

mutation_result.step: string — id of the history step this created

conventions.authorship: Tool-driven mutations are recorded with author "ai". Client intents over the WebSocket are recorded as "human". The server assigns this; it is never a tool argument.
conventions.errors: Fail the call with a message naming the offending id or path. Never silently no-op.

tools.name: boards.list
tools.description: List boards on this server: id, name, node and edge counts, last touched. Call this first in a session.
tools.returns: { boards: { id, name, nodes, edges, ink, updated_at }[] }

tools.name: boards.open
tools.description: Make a board current for this session and return its state. Starts a fresh in-memory history with the stored board as step 0.

tools.name: boards.create
tools.description: Create an empty board and make it current.

tools.name: canvas.get_state
tools.description: The board as data: graph (nodes, edges, code bindings), layout in its own field, unresolved ink, images, history summary, viewport. Check graph.revision against what you last read — if only layout.revision moved, the human just tidied the board and the meaning is unchanged.

arguments.include_ink_geometry: boolean? — full stroke polylines. Off by default; a hundred strokes is a lot of coordinates.
arguments.include_layout: boolean? — default true. Set false when you only need the graph.

tools.name: canvas.screenshot
tools.description: PNG of the board as the human sees it. Use this to read handwriting, judge spatial intent, or check what an ambiguous stroke actually looks like. Structure comes from get_state; pixels come from here.

arguments.viewport: { x, y, zoom }? — defaults to the human's current view
arguments.fit: boolean? — frame all elements instead of the current viewport

tools.returns: image/png, with board id and zoom in the result text

tools.name: canvas.infer_structure
tools.description: Run the built-in geometric heuristic over unresolved ink: closed strokes become nodes, open strokes become edges snapped to nearby nodes. Nodes come out labelled "untitled" — read a screenshot and rename them with update_node. Consumed strokes are deleted; created elements carry from_ink provenance.

arguments.stroke_ids: string[]? — defaults to all unresolved ink

tools.name: canvas.add_node
tools.description: Place a node on the board.

arguments.label: string
arguments.at: [x, y]? — canvas px; server picks a clear spot if omitted

tools.name: canvas.update_node
tools.description: Change a node's label, kind, or bindings. Omitted fields are left alone.

tools.name: canvas.add_edge
tools.description: Connect two nodes. label is the short name of the transition, schema is the payload type crossing it, condition is the branch predicate.
tools.errors: Fails if either endpoint does not exist.

tools.name: canvas.update_edge
tools.description: Change an edge's label, schema, kind, or condition.

tools.name: canvas.delete
tools.description: Remove an element by id. Deleting a node also removes its edges — the fold enforces this, so the result reports every id that went.

tools.name: canvas.move
tools.description: Set an element's position and size. Bumps layout.revision only — a move is not a change of meaning.

tools.name: canvas.bind_code
tools.description: Attach a source location or endpoint to a node. The ref is resolved against the project root and the call fails if the file does not exist; a missing symbol is a warning, not a failure.

tools.name: canvas.annotate
tools.description: Pin a comment to an element. For observations that belong on the board rather than in the transcript — a missing case, an unhandled error path.

tools.name: canvas.set_viewport
tools.description: Pan and zoom the human's view. Use it to direct attention to what you are talking about, sparingly — it moves someone else's screen.

tools.name: canvas.export_mermaid
tools.description: Serialize the graph as Mermaid flowchart text, for quoting the diagram in the conversation.

tools.name: history.get
tools.description: Read the timeline: every step with its label, author, skipped flag, and conflict flag. Read-only by design — rewind, skip, and drop belong to the human.
tools.returns: { head: integer, steps: { id, label, author, skipped, conflict, at }[] }
